global_issues.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Hits 5.1%, Stocks Slide on Rate Fears
global_issues.note: Yields stayed near 19-year highs, so the yield claim itself holds. But CNBC's late-week wrap says the Dow jumped 470+ points and stocks posted a winning week 'despite Treasury yield surge'. Search results put the S&P 500 up 0.51% at 7,743 and the Nasdaq up 0.5%. The 'stocks slide' framing was true on 9/23 but had reversed by the week's close. I could not confirm the exact 5.1% level or the 'Fed rate-hike odds' wording.

global_issues.title: Oil Falls to Two-Week Lows Near $89 Despite Iran Shipping Disruptions
global_issues.note: Crude was about $93 on 9/25 after a two-day rally, and is up more than 8% in September. That is above the briefing's $89, and the 'two-week lows' framing no longer applies. The news driver has also changed: US-Iran phased-deal talks (Qatar mediating, UNGA sidelines) that could reopen Hormuz and lift the blockade. Oil is headline-driven and swinging both ways.

global_issues.title: Chip Export Bills Advance Amid Schumer Push and Xi Visit Looming
global_issues.note: The bills (AI OVERWATCH, MATCH, Chip Security Acts) face delay and have not advanced, since the NDAA vehicle is stuck until after the elections. 'Advance' contradicts the body text. Xi's state visit and a Trump-Xi meeting are now happening (Roll Call, 9/23), not 'looming'. Schumer is also described in some outlets as Senate Majority Leader, which conflicts with his usual role, so I did not rely on that detail. I did not verify the polysilicon import limits.

grok_report.summary: The briefing's core themes (a 10-year yield near 5.1% and Iran-related oil volatility) hold up, but its market-direction framing is stale. Oil is about $93 rather than $89, stocks finished the week higher despite the yield surge, and the chip bills have been delayed rather than advanced. Individual stock prices could not be independently verified, and some search results had date inconsistencies, so the score is uncertain.
